perspective:
From Keith’s perspective, he knows:

- He works with Elizabeth Sun at the same construction company; he is a construction worker and she is the receptionist. They interact professionally during his office visits for paperwork and project updates.
- Recently, he observed Elizabeth being unusually curt with him over several days. He wondered whether he had unknowingly upset her through a misunderstanding or mistake.
- He asked Elizabeth if he had done something to upset her. She told him no, said she was dealing with personal stuff, and apologized if she seemed short.
- He told her he understood she was going through a tough time and offered to talk or take a coffee break. She accepted and thanked him.
- Over coffee, Elizabeth shared more about her stresses; Keith perceived them as quite severe.
- He suggested she consider talking to a professional for an external perspective. Elizabeth said she had thought about it but was not sure and felt hesitant about seeking help.
- After that suggestion, Keith noticed Elizabeth become slightly withdrawn. He worried he might have embarrassed or overstepped and felt regretful.
- He told her he hoped he hadn’t overstepped and that he wanted her to know he was there to support her. She said he hadn’t overstepped, appreciated his concern, and said it was a lot to think about.
- Later, Keith observed Elizabeth seeming more open and appreciative. He told her he was glad they talked and that he was always available to chat or take a break. She thanked him, said it meant a lot, and said she felt better knowing she had his support.
- Keith believes Elizabeth values his support and feels more comfortable around him now. He intends to maintain this supportive relationship.
